brief.headline: HBM4 ship cycle diverges as Samsung labor strike countdown accelerates; DRAM/NAND +58-75% QoQ Q2; hyperscaler capex revised to $725bn
brief.summary: <cite index="42-4,42-6">Samsung began HBM4 mass-production shipments in February 2026 while SK Hynix has confirmed HBM4 progress per customer agreements but made no comparable public announcement, with HBM4E mass production targeted for 2027.</cite> <cite index="41-15,41-16,41-17">Samsung's union announced an 18-day walkout May 21-June 7, with KB Securities estimating disruption of 3-4% global DRAM supply and 2-3% NAND, with losses of ~₩1tn/day and prolonged action risking Nvidia client defection.</cite> <cite index="11-1,16-1">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 following Q1's record 90-95% surge, while NAND jumped 70-75% QoQ, outpacing DRAM for the first time this cycle.</cite> <cite index="27-1,27-5">Hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates now stand at $725bn, nearly double the $365bn consensus from one year ago, with memory consuming ~30% of total spend.</cite> <cite index="5-7,5-11">Samsung confirmed conventional DRAM profitability now exceeds HBM due to quarterly vs. annual pricing negotiation lag, with conventional DRAM prices surging each quarter while HBM locked at year-start rates.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="47-21,47-22">SK Hynix 2026 forward PER overtook Samsung for the first time at 6.79x vs. 6.77x, reversing a 2.8-point gap from three months ago.</cite> <cite index="47-20">SK Hynix returned 78.68% over the past month vs. Samsung's 35.44%, more than double.</cite> <cite index="42-10,42-11">Samsung holds ~40% DRAM share and is shipping HBM4 for Nvidia's Vera Rubin program; any strike-driven delivery interruption risks pushing hyperscalers toward SK Hynix, which controls ~57% of the HBM market.</cite> <cite index="44-14,44-15,44-18">Valuation flip marks the first time SK Hynix forward PER surpassed Samsung; with SK Hynix now more expensive on near-term earnings, market expectations for the two have converged.</cite> Trade: long Samsung/short SK Hynix on strike resolution, valuation gap closure, and HBM4 qualification lead; reverse if strike extends or Hynix announces HBM4 volume ramp ahead of Samsung's Q2 guide.

memory_cycle.stage: Late up-cycle with peak pricing mechanics
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-3,16-6,16-7">Structural shift has deepened; memory producers prioritize HBM over conventional DRAM as long as AI infrastructure buildouts continue, and every quarter without new capacity locks in higher prices for the next cycle.</cite> <cite index="16-9">$755bn in 2026 hyperscaler capex (with memory ~30% of total) is a structural demand floor that did not exist in prior cycles.</cite> <cite index="16-13,16-16,16-17">No credible near-term relief scenario; new fab capacity not expected to reach meaningful volume before late 2027 or 2028.</cite> <cite index="4-1,4-13">Industry forecasts suggest meeting only ~60% of DRAM demand by 2027 as HBM4 12-layer shipments ramp.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="42-14,42-15,42-16">Samsung's HBM4 built on 6th-gen 1c DRAM with 4nm logic base die delivers 11.7 Gbps, 46% above JEDEC 8 Gbps standard; Samsung expects total HBM sales to more than triple in 2026 vs. 2025.</cite> <cite index="8-14,8-16">HBM4 mass production now expected late Q1 2026/early Q2 2026 across suppliers following Nvidia Rubin spec revision to >11 Gbps per-pin.</cite> <cite index="8-5,8-6">Samsung took early lead by adopting 1Cnm process and advanced in-house foundry tech for base die, positioning as most likely to qualify first for higher-end Rubin products.</cite> <cite index="5-1,5-2,5-5">Conventional DRAM now overtakes HBM profitability due to pricing lag; Samsung offers 'balanced product mix,' SK Hynix points to 'redesigning LTA structure.'</cite> <cite index="4-1">More cautious forecasts suggest industry may meet only ~60% of DRAM demand by 2027 as 12-layer HBM4 shipments ramp.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Samsung begins HBM4 mass shipments in February; SK Hynix targets HBM4E for 2027
news_pulse.implication: Samsung gains 6-month HBM4 product cycle lead; SK Hynix focusing on higher-margin HBM4E next year. Strike risk may erode Samsung's time-to-market advantage if prolonged.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung union announces 18-day strike May 21-June 7; ₩1tn/day loss estimated
news_pulse.implication: KB Securities: 3-4% global DRAM supply, 2-3% NAND at risk. JPMorgan: >₩40tn annual op profit hit. April half-day rally cut memory output 18.4%, foundry 58%. Nvidia client defection risk elevates SK Hynix relative positioning.

news_pulse.headline: Conventional DRAM profitability surpasses HBM for first time; Samsung/Hynix diverge on response
news_pulse.implication: Quarterly conventional DRAM pricing outpaced annual HBM LTAs locked at start-of-year rates. Samsung pursuing 'balanced product mix'; SK Hynix 'redesigning LTA structure' to lock multi-year volumes with pricing floors. Shift may accelerate HBM capacity pivot if pricing structures converge.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract +58-63% QoQ Q2, NAND +70-75%; Q1 saw record +90-95% DRAM, +55-60% NAND
news_pulse.implication: NAND outpaces DRAM for first time this cycle as enterprise SSD demand absorbs capacity. PC DRAM momentum slowed but remains elevated; rate of increase decelerating from Q1 extreme base. Supply crunch unlikely to ease before 2H 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725bn, up from $365bn consensus one year ago; memory ~30% of total
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft ~$150bn annualized, Amazon ~$200bn, Alphabet ~$185bn, Meta ~$135bn. 2027 estimates now >$1tn. Memory structural demand floor underpins pricing through 2028. Hyperscalers locking multi-year LTAs, absorbing available supply before open market.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity targeting 130k wafers/month by late 2026, up from 75-80k in late 2025
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia secures ~60% of 2026 CoWoS capacity. CoWoS yield at 98%; Gen 3 accommodates 12 HBM stacks, Gen 5 (by 2029) targets 24 stacks. Outsourcing 240-270k wafers/year to Amkor/SPIL. Packaging bottleneck easing but HBM supply remains constraint.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix forward PER overtakes Samsung for first time at 6.79x vs. 6.77x
news_pulse.implication: Valuation convergence after SK Hynix 1-month return of 78.68% vs. Samsung 35.44%. Gap was 2.8 points three months ago. Analysts: heavier valuation on Hynix could support Samsung relative strength near-term. YTD: Samsung +125.6%, SK Hynix +179.4% as of May 15.

news_pulse.headline: Micron CEO: AI memory demand 'first innings,' industry may meet only 60% of DRAM demand by 2027
news_pulse.implication: HBM4 12-layer ramp in earnest; supply crunch extends through 2028 given fab lead times. Stopgap fixes (older GPUs with more VRAM, mixed DDR5 setups) emerging. Consumer IT 'shrinkflation' spreading as AI absorbs commodity DRAM/NAND capacity.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="41-7,41-8">Pre-market May 14: Samsung 005930.KS at ₩286k (+0.70%), SK Hynix 000660.KS at ₩1.996m (+1.01%), approaching ₩2m threshold never previously closed above.</cite> <cite index="46-21">SK Hynix 2x leveraged ETF (7709.HK) AUM ~$5.4bn, world's largest single-stock leveraged product; Samsung 2x (7747.HK) ~$1.65bn.</cite> <cite index="41-4,41-5,41-6">Trump-Xi Beijing summit (began May 13) covering semiconductor export controls, tariffs, rare earths, Taiwan, Iran, AI—direct catalyst for rally.</cite> Options signal: elevated strike risk premium in Samsung near-term puts; Hynix call skew reflecting momentum but valuation cap. Watch ₩2m psychological level on Hynix and ₩300k on Samsung as technical magnets.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung labor court injunction ruling (Suwon District Court) — any decision grants/denies strike legal protections; union participation count May 21
SK Hynix HBM4 customer qualification announcements — any public confirmation of Nvidia/AMD/Google design wins vs. Samsung's disclosed shipments
Hyperscaler earnings call transcripts (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN) — specific memory budget splits between HBM4/conventional DRAM, LTA structure commentary
TSMC CoWoS monthly capacity update and Nvidia/Broadcom/AMD 2H allocation leaks — any reallocation signals Samsung strike contingency
DRAM spot price movement post-strike announcement — DDR5/LPDDR5X spot premiums if buyers frontrun Samsung supply disruption
